query: What limitation of the current Nest bot motivates the AI assistant project?
reference: Nest bot only responds to pre-programmed commands, so it cannot answer general or project-related questions, leading to unresolved queries and repeated manual answering by members.
contexts: Nest bot currently operates based on commands and can only respond to data tied to each command.
Users frequently ask general or project-specific questions that don't match any existing command.
When Nest bot can't answer these queries, manual guidance is needed, sometimes leaving questions unsolved or repeatedly answered.

query: What is Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and why is it used in the Nest bot project?
reference: RAG improves LLM responses by retrieving relevant information from an external knowledge base before generating an answer, making replies more accurate and context-aware for OWASP-specific queries.
contexts: RAG enhances LLM responses by pulling relevant information from an external knowledge base before generating an answer.
Without RAG the LLM only relies on what it was trained on; with RAG, retrieved context plus the query are both given to the model.
The technique is used so OWASP-specific answers stay accurate and context-aware.

query: How does the Nest bot proposal use Redis caching, and what does the distance_threshold control?
reference: Redis stores previously generated RAG/LLM responses and uses semantic search to match new queries to cached ones; the distance_threshold (0.2-0.4) controls how strict or flexible that semantic match is.
contexts: Redis caches the RAG plus LLM generated response so it can be reused for similar future questions.
Semantic search compares embeddings of the new query against cached query embeddings using a distance_threshold of 0.2 to 0.4.
A lower distance_threshold makes the semantic match stricter, while a higher one allows more flexible matching.

query: Describe the multi-layered approach used to route user queries to the correct Slack channel.
reference: The first layer is a rule-based keyword match with a longest-match-first strategy; if ambiguous, a second layer uses TF-IDF features with a trained classifier to predict the channel, falling back to RAG below a confidence threshold.
contexts: The rule-based layer defines keywords, abbreviations, and synonyms to identify which channel to route to.
A Longest Match First strategy favors the most specific matching keyword when multiple keywords match.
If ambiguity remains, a second layer combining TF-IDF and a trained classifier is used to refine channel prediction.
Predictions below the confidence threshold are passed to the RAG pipeline instead of suggesting a channel.

query: Which classifier algorithms will be compared for the channel-routing model, and how will the best one be chosen?
reference: Multinomial Logistic Regression, Linear SVM, and Multinomial Naive Bayes will be trained on TF-IDF vectors and compared using accuracy, F1 score, and precision/recall to select the best performer.
contexts: Classifiers considered include Multinomial Logistic Regression, Linear Support Vector Machine, and Multinomial Naive Bayes trained on TF-IDF vectors.
The evaluation uses metrics such as accuracy_score, F1 score, and precision/recall to determine which model performs best.
A/B testing across these classifiers helps select the most accurate one for the project's needs.

query: What frameworks are combined to build the RAG pipeline in the Nest bot proposal, and how do they differ?
reference: LangChain and LangGraph are combined; LangChain builds linear execution chains, while LangGraph, part of LangChain, allows defining graph-based workflows with conditional nodes and edges.
contexts: The RAG pipeline combines LangChain, a framework for linear execution chains, with LangGraph.
LangGraph allows defining graph workflows using conditional nodes and edges instead of simple linear chains.

query: What monitoring and observability tool does the Nest bot proposal plan to self-host, and what metrics does it track?
reference: Signoz, an open-source observability tool, is self-hosted via Docker and used to track pipeline latency, cache hit rate, and LLM response time.
contexts: Signoz is an open-source tool used to get logs, metrics, and performance details of the RAG pipeline, self-hosted via a Dockerfile.
Tracked metrics include pipeline latency, cache hit rate, and LLM response time, used to tune thresholds and improve performance.

query: What mechanism does the Nest bot proposal use to validate the LLM's generated answers before showing them to users?
reference: The generated response is compared against the retrieved text_content; if it isn't relevant it's sent back to the LLM for refinement, and a carefully written prompt template also aims to reduce hallucinations or informal answers.
contexts: The response generated by the LLM is verified by comparing it with the retrieved text_content from the database.
If the answer is not relevant, it is sent back to the LLM for refinement based on the data source.
A proper prompt template helps ensure the validation layer avoids hallucinations or informal answers.

query: What are the deliverables listed for the OWASP Nest bot AI assistant GSoC 2025 project?
reference: The deliverables are a classifier model trained on OWASP data, a new AI-capable Nest bot, a tested production-ready mechanism for it, and usage documentation.
contexts: Deliverables include developing a classifier model trained on OWASP's data.
A new Nest bot with AI assistance capabilities is a deliverable.
Testing and a production-ready mechanism for the Nest bot AI assistant, plus usage documentation, are also listed.

query: How does the Nest bot proposal plan to keep improving the caching layer over time without it becoming bloated?
reference: An automated weekly or bi-weekly job fetches and stores positively-rated cached responses, and responses are discarded once they accumulate enough negative feedback.
contexts: A method fetches positive cached responses and stores them in the database, run via an automated job weekly or bi-weekly.
The count of positive and negative feedback is stored so cached responses can be discarded after enough negative feedback accumulates.
This keeps the caching layer from growing too large while still returning fast responses.
